verifiedBehavior: Expired token with known issuer/client/scopes in the actual credential envelope refreshes once after a real grant, publishes intent/final immutable slots, initializes once, executes two distinct tools and continues Context/model under unchanged grant facts; next request receives its own live Host port.

Epoch binds full execution identity and registry. Only private OAuth publication owner can advance actual Store revision; normalized credential-source identity applies only when current Store is exactly that owned generation. Goal/args/policy/lease/ancestry/role/registry and foreign credential mutations retain live checks. Epoch contains no secrets and is never serialized as permission truth.

A naturally expiring token during a real 16-second tool call causes old Connection close/join before a second refresh and new initialize; two token exchanges, two initializes, two tools. Bound redaction carries used prior access tokens/proxy credentials and original refresh credentials across generations; untrusted old/new token echoes never enter Tool Result, model Context or Evidence.

Denied expired OAuth reads neither Helper nor IdP and leaves metadata bytes unchanged. Policy revocation during sent refresh persists actual token but prevents tool initialization; registry/foreign credential mutations preserve pending/foreign data and prevent tool dispatch. No credential operation alone creates tool unknown.

Scope expansion and narrowing both preserve pending and block initialization; following tool request sees recovery_required and does not repeat refresh. Missing actual issuer/client/scope/refresh binding requires explicit authorization rather than DCR or browser automation.

TERM during automatic token exchange preserves intent, confirms tool not_dispatched, closes the owner and leaves zero tool uncertain dispatches. Explicit new code authorization then admits a later canonical native task with actual ToolResult/Evidence while old conversation stays unchanged.

KILL during token exchange leaves orphan credential lock. Canonical recovery retains unfenced_external tool uncertainty because credential pending is not proof of no tool dispatch; old tool is never replayed, metadata/history retained and further admission blocked.

Actual encrypted Vault/lock with synthetic key participates in runtime refresh and real grant/tool/evidence/model closure. HTTP(S) authenticated CONNECT tests require each OAuth request numeric while ordinary MCP retains configured hostname routing; proxy auth does not reach origin. Existing stdio/Streamable JSON/SSE/legacy SSE, denial, initialization revocation, deadlines, loss/unknown and stop tests pass.

Logical per-server owner has eight queue entries and bounded pool; each command owns its current Host admission port. Stdio is never auto-restarted. An execution_outcome_unknown RPC or protection-overflow stops the owner; cancellation/stop waits actual Connection/SDK/worker cleanup, and unproven stop remains unknown.
